name: Zhou Jianhe
current_role: President, Junefield (Holdings) Ltd (Hong Kong); chairman, Prime Century Investments Ltd (per MarketScreener, undated)
profile: Hong Kong-based businessman (also styled Zhou Chu Jian He) behind Junefield Group, whose interests span Beijing property, hospitality and trade. name: Dmitry Troitsky
current_role: Co-owner and board director, O'KEY Group / DA Group (Russian grocery retail; re-elected to board May 2026)
profile: St Petersburg entrepreneur, Leningrad Shipbuilding Institute graduate, who with longtime partner Dmitry Korzhev co-founded juice maker Multon (sold to Coca-Cola) and in 2001 the O'KEY supermarket chain, listed in London in 2010. After O'KEY sold its hypermarkets in 2025 the group runs the DA! discounter and is being renamed DA Group.
interesting_fact: He and Korzhev built Multon juice plant from 1995 and sold it to Coca-Cola about ten years later for roughly $500m, funding the O'KEY supermarket chain.
deep_cut_fact: He and Korzhev began working together as students; their first venture was selling cars, which became Mega-Auto (1993), one of St Petersburg's largest car dealers.
notes: Low media profile; Russia-based, sanctions/compliance context worth checking before outreach. Board re-election: https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/117810/ . Input lists 'fashion-retail' but he is grocery retail (O'KEY).

name: Hu Dong
current_role: Founder, Chairman, CEO and CFO, Ebang International Holdings (Nasdaq: EBON), Hangzhou
profile: Born 1973; founded Hangzhou-based Ebang, which started out making communications network access equipment and around 2014 pivoted into bitcoin-mining ASIC machines, listing on Nasdaq in 2020. Holds most of the voting power; Ebang has since expanded into crypto exchange, payments and mining businesses.
interesting_fact: Ebang began as a telecom network-equipment maker and only moved into blockchain/bitcoin-mining hardware around 2014, becoming one of China's big three miner makers.
deep_cut_fact: Before and while building Ebang he was a lecturer at Zhejiang University of Technology's College of Computer Science and Technology (where he earned an industrial automation degree in 1998); he also holds a Zhejiang University MBA and Tsinghua EMBA.
notes: Strong fit for data-center/energy angle (bitcoin-mining hardware, mining operations). Company was subject of a 2020 Hindenburg short report. IR contacts from 2023 releases; confirm on latest release.

name: Chen Zhifeng
current_role: Chairman, Yema (Wild Horse) Group Co., Ltd., Urumqi, Xinjiang
profile: Xinjiang entrepreneur whose Yema Group grew from trade with Central Asia into finance, property and tourism (Hurun China 2008-2014). He is best known as the man who brought Akhal-Teke 'heavenly horses' from Central Asia to China in numbers, running a breeding and exhibition base in Urumqi (Xinjiang Paleo-ecology Park).
interesting_fact: Claims the world's largest herd of Akhal-Teke horses, more than 300, imported from Turkmenistan via Kazakhstan to his ranch in Urumqi.
deep_cut_fact: He bred the first Akhal-Teke foal born in China and founded the country's first Akhal-Teke exhibition base; at the 2016 Huanta Rally in Tacheng he had the horses pay tribute at the opening ceremony.
notes: Horse/Silk-Road angle is the best hook. No official Yema Group website or contacts found in this pass.

name: Peter Beckwith
current_role: Chairman, PMB Holdings Ltd (private property/investment company, since 1992)
profile: British property entrepreneur (b. 1945) who in 1971 co-founded London & Edinburgh Trust with his brother Sir John Beckwith, building it into one of the UK's top ten property companies. Since 1992 he has run PMB Holdings, whose projects include a Westminster council JV on 90-104 Berwick Street, Soho. Honorary Fellow of Emmanuel College, Cambridge, OBE.
interesting_fact: Co-founded London & Edinburgh Trust with brother John in 1971 and made it one of the UK's top ten real estate companies.
deep_cut_fact: A keen Old Harrovian footballer: he played in the Old Harrovians AFC's first-ever Arthur Dunn Cup tie (Jan 1967, lost 3-2 in the last seconds of extra time), went on the club's first Easter tour to Etretat in 1964 and only hung up his boots at 44.
notes: Read Law at Emmanuel College, Cambridge (Honorary Fellow; profile https://www.emma.cam.ac.uk/about/contact/fellows/?id=131); long-time Harrow School governor; chairs the Vivien and Peter Beckwith Young Musicians Trust (charity 1015344). No published direct contact found; charity register is a possible formal route.

name: William Arah
current_role: Co-founder, Director and Portfolio Manager (Japan), Marathon Asset Management, London
profile: Oxford MA who entered investment management in 1982 and co-founded London's Marathon Asset Management in 1986, the long-only firm known for 'capital cycle' investing. He has managed Marathon's Japanese equities since 1987, sits on the board and Partners Group, and remains a named PM on its Japan, EAFE and ACWI ex-US strategies.
interesting_fact: Has run Marathon's Japanese equity portfolios continuously since 1987, nearly four decades, making him one of the longest-serving Japan PMs in London.

public_contacts.value: https://www.marathon.co.uk (Marathon; also runs an Insights & Podcast section)

notes: Low public profile. A search summary mentioned an early stint on Rowe & Pitman's Japan desk in Tokyo (1983) and Goldman Sachs, but I could not verify it on a primary page, so it is not used. Marathon's capital-cycle framework (books 'Capital Account'/'Capital Returns') is a natural podcast hook.

name: Wang Xuehai
current_role: Former chairman/director, Humanwell Healthcare (人福医药); a principal of Wuhan Dangdai Technology Industries Group (current role unconfirmed)
profile: Wuhan entrepreneur associated with Wuhan Dangdai Technology Industries Group, a conglomerate in pharmaceuticals, real estate, education and travel whose flagship was Shanghai-listed Humanwell Healthcare, which he chaired. Dangdai lost control of Humanwell in 2025 when China Merchants' life-science arm reorganised its board, ending 32 years of Dangdai control.
interesting_fact: Humanwell, which he chaired, grew into one of China's leading anaesthesia/analgesia drug makers under Dangdai's 32-year control before China Merchants took over in 2025.
notes: Sensitive: Dangdai group has been in financial distress and he was named in regulatory penalties (SSE 2023, Hubei CSRC Dec 2025) over related-party fund occupation at Humanwell; avoid referencing. Humanwell IR (board secretary) is the only corporate route, but he is no longer in control.

name: Tang Qiu
current_role: Chairman, legal representative and co-controlling shareholder, Shenzhen Ysstech Info-tech (赢时胜, SZSE: 300377)
profile: Born 1971; an engineer who in 2001 began running Ysstech, the Shenzhen financial-IT firm (founded 1998) whose asset-management accounting/valuation and custody software is used by 300+ banks, brokers, trusts and insurers, with a claimed >90% domestic share in its core niche. Chairman since 2010; the firm listed on ChiNext in 2014 and is pushing into cloud, big data, AI and blockchain.
